citations.description: Ticket comment by RebarBotNava: 'AC#2 is NOT satisfiable through this integration test — verified at runtime, not assumed. ... a seeded unconditional-stamp mutation left the test GREEN.'

findings.criterion: With the patch in place, making `clear_absent` stamp `updated_at` unconditionally drives the integration test RED — verified by seeding that mutation, not assumed.
findings.detail: The implementation agent verified at runtime that this criterion is not satisfiable through this integration test. `clear_absent` is never reached on a healthy in-window pass because its two call sites (`binding_walk.py:254` and `outbound_differ.py:675`) are gated on out-of-window-but-alive keys, and the idempotency fixture seeds all keys in-window. A seeded unconditional-stamp mutation was confirmed to leave the test GREEN. No code change was made to satisfy this criterion. The ticket comment documents this as a false premise in AC#2 and recommends either accepting the existing unit-tier guard as sufficient or filing a separate harness-extension story.
findings.remediation: Either (a) accept AC#1 hardening + the existing unit-tier guard (`test_clear_absent_does_not_dirty_an_entry_with_no_absence`) as sufficient and reclassify/drop AC#2; or (b) file a separate ticket to extend the integration harness to wire the fake into the Backend port and add an out-of-window fixture so the bound-but-absent-alive path executes, enabling a true mutation-RED test.
findings.title: AC#2: mutation-RED verification not achievable

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
